root_cause: Text.append(text) and Text.append_text(text) do self._spans.extend(generator over text._spans). When text is self, the generator iterates the same list it is extending, so it never ends. It only triggers when the Text has a style (or existing spans): append first pushes a style Span onto self._spans (== text._spans), so the list is non-empty and every yielded span adds one more. With an unstyled, span-less Text the list is empty and nothing hangs.
best_solution: Take a snapshot of the source spans before extending: iterate over text._spans.copy() (list(...) or tuple(...) work too) in BOTH Text.append (Text branch) and Text.append_text. Both methods use the same extend-from-generator code, so both have the bug. The linked issue only shows a.append(a), so the reasoning goes: find every place that extends self._spans from text._spans (grep '_spans.extend' / 'for start, end, style in text._spans') and fix each one.
acceptable_alternatives: list(text._spans) / tuple(text._spans) / text._spans[:] in both methods; or detect `text is self` and copy first. A fix that touches only append() fails, because the hidden test also calls append_text on self.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_text.py::test_append_loop_regression: a=Text('one','blue'); a.append(a); a.plain=='oneone'; and b=Text('two','blue'); b.append_text(b); b.plain=='twotwo'. Both must finish; the style argument is what triggers the loop. Only .plain is checked, not the spans.
locating_signals: Title 'fix infinite loop in append' plus the issue link. The issue text (not in the statement) shows a.append(a) with style 'blue'. The word 'append' leads to Text.append in rich/text.py. append_text is not named anywhere, so you only find it by grepping for the same pattern. The statement is just a PR title plus a link.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass false). v4, v6 and v7 each ran a repro one-liner with a styled Text (Text('foo', style='bold').append(t)). It hung until the ~180 s command timeout, used half the 6-minute session, and then got run AGAIN. The session timed out. v6 and v7 submitted empty patches. v4's patch held only a reproduce_issue.py script, even though its explanation had found the root cause. v8 fixed only Text.append (tuple(text._spans)) and missed the identical loop in Text.append_text. The hidden test's append_text half still loops forever, so the run hit a test timeout (exit 124). v8 also added a stray tests/test_append_self.py.
generalizable_lesson: (1) When the bug is a hang or infinite loop, always put a hard timeout on repro commands (e.g. `timeout 10 python -c ...`). Treat a timeout as confirming the bug, and never re-run a command that already hung. (2) After fixing a pattern bug such as mutating a collection while iterating it, or aliasing self with an argument, grep the module for every copy of that pattern (sibling methods like append/append_text, add/add_all, extend/extend_many) and fix each one. Hidden tests often check the sibling. (3) If the statement is just a title plus an issue link, get the concrete trigger (here, a style argument) into the repro, because the simple case does not reproduce.
